newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saybolt experts in Iraq to inspect oil metering gear.
newsitem.headline: Saybolt experts in Iraq to inspect oil metering gear.

text.p: Two experts from the Dutch firm Saybolt arrived in Baghdad on Tuesday to see whether Iraq's oil gauging equipment on the border with Turkey was working properly.
The experts -- one British, John Stokes and the other Dutch, Debruijn Huibregt -- declined comment on arrival.
A U.N. source in Baghdad said on Tuesday the two would meet officials from Iraq's State Organisation for the Marketing of Oil (SOMO) before heading to northern Iraq on Wednesday.
They will inspect Iraq's twin pipeline via Turkey to ensure faulty equipment at the Zakho station near the Turkish border is now operational.

The visit by Saybolt experts is part of preparations for the imminent flow of partial Iraqi exports worth $2 billion in six months under an oil-for-food deal with U.N. whose terms Baghdad accepted on November 25.
The United Nations on Monday said that the inspection by Saybolt was the last step before the oil-for-food deal could start running.

A team from Lloyd's Shipping Intelligence left Baghdad on Tuesday following an inspection tour of Iraq's trade outlets with the outside world to pave the way for future U.N. inspection of humanitarian supplies reaching Iraq under the oil deal.
The experts visited Umm Qasr port on the Gulf and the border post in Zakho. The U.N. source in Baghdad said they would inspect the border post of Treibeel on the Iraq-Jordan border on their way home.
